item: quality pass on 3.3 (finding, does not block any item)
question: tools/branches-editor.html, the tool CLAUDE.md tells everyone to use for editing branches.json, carries a full embedded copy of branches.json inside itself as a starting snapshot. If someone opens the editor, changes one branch and hits Download without first hitting Load a branches.json, they get the snapshot plus their one change, not the current file, and every edit made since the snapshot was taken is silently reverted. The download also stamps today's date into lastUpdated, so the stale export looks like the newest file. The snapshot was one edit behind when this run found it and has been refreshed by hand to match, but hand-refreshing it after every edit is a treadmill rather than a fix. How should the editor be made safe?
options: Make the editor refuse to download until a branches.json has been loaded in that session, so an export can never be built on the snapshot. Smallest change, removes the failure mode entirely, and the snapshot stays useful for read-only browsing
Strip the embedded snapshot out and have the editor open empty with a Load prompt. Removes the stale copy altogether, but the editor stops being a quick way to look at the data without a file to hand

Leave the behaviour alone and keep refreshing the snapshot by hand whenever branches.json changes. No code change, but it depends on every future editor remembering, and the failure is silent when they forget
answer: Recommended option (1): the editor now refuses to Download until a real branches.json has been loaded that session. Answered and implemented directly by Rishi in a Cowork session on 2026-08-09 rather than left for a worker run, since Rishi is stepping away for the next 24 hours and wanted it closed out immediately. Download now checks a loadedFromFile flag, set only by a successful Load; Save shows an explanatory alert and returns early if it is false, instead of silently exporting the bundled snapshot. All five checkers re-run clean afterwards (177 pages, 262 text files, 16 branches, 0 failures).
note: Nothing is blocked by this and nothing about the current data is wrong: the snapshot has been brought level with branches.json as part of this run. It is raised because it is the one route by which a single careless click could undo the whole audit backlog's data work on the single source of truth, and because CLAUDE.md's own rule is that stale copies of branches.json are a hazard. Option 1 is recommended because it is a few lines in one file and it makes the safe path the only path.

question: A generated service page no longer carries its own booking widget id: it ships an empty box and modules/service/service.js reads the live URL, looks the branch up in branches.json and renders the right Appointedd diary. That design has a deliberate safety rule inside it. If a page's own service has no widget id, service.js falls back to the branch's Pharmacy First diary, except for weight loss and travel clinic, which are barred from falling back because they are separate services with their own diaries and a booking landing in the wrong one is worse than no booking at all. The NHS Pharmacy Contraception Service is in exactly that position, and it was left out of the bar: it has its own diary at all 14 branches that offer it, it is never the Pharmacy First diary anywhere, and no branch's Pharmacy First overview page links to it. Nothing is wrong today, because a contraception page is only generated where the branch already holds a contraception widget, so the fallback never fires. The reason this is a question rather than a two-word fix is that service.js is a CDN-pinned asset, and it is currently byte-identical between main and the pinned branch service-module-phase1. Q13's recommended fix, fast-forwarding that pinned branch to main, is free precisely because nothing has diverged yet. Changing service.js now would end that. item: quality pass on 3.12 (finding, does not block any item)
question: branches.json holds two names for every branch: brandLabel, the brand ("Scorah Chemists"), and branchName, this particular shop ("Scorah Chemists Hazel Grove"). For ten of the sixteen branches they are the same string, so nothing turns on the choice. For six of them they are not, and those six are exactly the branches that share a brand and a website with a sister shop: Fishlocks Ainsdale and Eccleston, McCanns Aigburth and Sandringham, Scorah Bramhall and Hazel Grove. Five of the six generators reach for brandLabel and use it in two machine-readable places on every page they build: the JSON-LD "name", which is what Google reads to decide whether two addresses are one business or two, and the data-branch attribute, which service.js and switch.js read to label an enquiry, a callback request and a WhatsApp message. The sixth generator, build-branch-landing-pages, uses branchName. So on each of the three shared domains Google is handed twelve pages naming a Pharmacy at one postcode and twelve naming the same Pharmacy at another, plus one landing page each that does name the shop, and an enquiry from either shop arrives labelled with a name that fits both. Which name should the pages carry?
options: Move the five service-family generators onto branchName for the JSON-LD name and the data-branch attribute, leaving every visible line of copy on the brand as it reads today. Only the six shared-brand branches change, 72 pages in total; the other 105 pages regenerate byte-identical because their branchName and brandLabel are the same string. It makes the five generators agree with the landing-page generator that already does this, and it costs a Weebly repaste of 72 pages that are already in the paste queue

Change data-branch only and leave the JSON-LD name on the brand. Fixes the label on every enquiry, callback and WhatsApp message without altering anything Google reads, so there is no search consequence to weigh, but it leaves two Pharmacy records sharing one name on each of the three shared domains, which is the position item 2.2 was created to correct

Leave both fields as they are and record it as accepted, on the basis that the six shops trade under three brands and should present that way. No regeneration and no repaste, but each sister pair keeps competing for its town under one shared name, and an enquiry keeps arriving with a pharmacy label that names two shops
note: Nothing is blocked by this and nothing a patient reads is wrong: every visible line on all 78 pages names the right brand, at the right address, with the right phone number, and all sixteen checkers pass. Two details worth having before deciding. First, no enquiry is actually lost today, because the hidden website_url field carries the page URL on every submission, so the town can always be recovered by reading it; the ambiguity is in the human-readable label a helpdesk reads first, not in the data. Second, the switch pages are the sharper case: the page bakes a town-specific source value ("Fishlocks Chemist Ainsdale Switch Page"), and switch.js overwrites it with "Callback request - " plus data-branch the moment a visitor toggles callback mode, so on those six pages a correct label is actively replaced by an ambiguous one, and for a prescription switch the town is the thing that decides which shop sets the patient up. Raised rather than taken under the autonomous window on the same reading as Q13 to Q17: the window converts a decision that BLOCKS a worklist item into an autonomous one, and this blocks nothing, while option 0 changes how Google resolves six business entities and adds 72 pages to the paste run. New tools/check-branch-identity.js guards the whole question from now on and records the six branches in its KNOWN list against this question, so it reports every run without going permanently red, and the entry for a branch fails the run the moment that branch is fixed, so the list cannot rot. Eleven rules negative-tested and all eleven fired.
